The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) concluded in 2021 that a safe intake level could not be established due to concerns about possible DNA damage, and it has been banned as a food additive in the EU, while other authorities (such as in the U.S.) still allow it. Occasional exposure at typical food levels is unlikely to cause acute harm, but from a precautionary, health‑focused perspective, minimizing regular intake is reasonable, especially for children.","category":"colorant"}

monocalcium phosphate__food.analysis: {"name":"Monocalcium phosphate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A leavening agent and acidity regulator commonly used in baked goods; generally recognized as safe at typical food levels.","details":"Monocalcium phosphate provides a source of acid that reacts with baking soda to help doughs and batters rise, and it also helps control pH. It is widely used and well studied, and normal dietary exposure is considered safe for most people. Very high total phosphate intake from many processed foods may be a concern for individuals with kidney disease or impaired phosphate handling, who are often advised to limit phosphate additives overall.","category":"leavening agent"}

enzymes__food.analysis: {"name":"Enzymes","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Proteins that catalyze specific reactions in food processing (such as improving texture or shelf life); generally safe, though they can be occupational allergens.","details":"Food enzymes (such as amylases, proteases, or lipases) are used in tiny amounts to modify starches, proteins, or fats during manufacturing and are usually inactivated by heat. Regulatory agencies typically evaluate them for safety, and they are considered safe for consumers at the levels used in foods. However, workers exposed to enzyme powders can develop respiratory allergies, and people with very specific allergies (e.g., to certain microbial or fungal sources) may rarely react, though this is uncommon in the general population.","category":"processing aid"}

locust bean gum__food.analysis: {"name":"Locust bean gum","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A plant‑derived thickener and stabilizer from carob tree seeds; generally safe, with occasional digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals at high intakes.","details":"Locust bean gum (carob bean gum, E410) is a soluble fiber used to thicken and stabilize foods like ice cream, sauces, and dairy products. It is not digested in the small intestine and is fermented by gut bacteria, which can cause gas or bloating in some people when consumed in large amounts. Overall, it is considered safe, and its fiber content may even support bowel regularity, though infants and people with very sensitive digestion may need to be cautious with concentrated sources.","category":"thickener/stabilizer"}

dipotassium phosphate__food.analysis: {"name":"Dipotassium phosphate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A buffering agent and stabilizer that helps control acidity and improve texture in foods; generally safe at typical dietary levels, with caution for those with kidney issues.","details":"Dipotassium phosphate (E340) is used to regulate pH, act as an emulsifier, and stabilize proteins in products like creamers and processed dairy. For healthy individuals, intake at normal food levels is considered safe, but it contributes to total dietary phosphate load. People with chronic kidney disease or those advised to limit phosphate additives may need to reduce consumption of foods containing phosphate salts, including dipotassium phosphate.","category":"stabilizer/buffering agent"}

chocolate liquor__food.analysis: {"name":"Chocolate liquor","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Chocolate liquor is the ground, liquefied mass of cocoa beans containing cocoa solids and cocoa butter. It is generally safe but can be high in calories and may contain caffeine and theobromine.","details":"Chocolate liquor is the base ingredient for dark and milk chocolate and naturally contains cocoa solids, cocoa butter, and small amounts of stimulants like caffeine and theobromine. For most people it is safe in moderate amounts, but sensitive individuals (to caffeine, migraines, or reflux) may need to limit intake. It can also contain trace amounts of heavy metals (like cadmium or lead) depending on sourcing, which is a concern mainly with very high, frequent consumption of certain cocoa products.","category":"cocoa / chocolate"}

defatted soy flour__food.analysis: {"name":"Defatted soy flour","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Defatted soy flour is made from soybeans with most of the oil removed, leaving a high-protein flour. It is nutritious but is a major allergen and contains soy isoflavones, which may be a concern for some people.","details":"Defatted soy flour is used to boost protein and improve texture in baked goods and processed foods; it is rich in protein and fiber but also contains antinutrients (like trypsin inhibitors) that are mostly reduced by heat processing. Soy is a common allergen and can trigger reactions ranging from mild to severe in sensitive individuals. For most people, moderate intake is considered safe, but those with soy allergy, thyroid issues, or who must limit phytoestrogens should be cautious and consult a healthcare professional.","category":"soy / legume"}

milk__food.analysis: {"name":"Milk","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Milk is a dairy ingredient providing protein, fat, and lactose sugar. It is a major allergen and can cause issues for people with milk allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"Milk and milk-derived ingredients are common in many processed foods and contribute calcium, protein, and saturated fat. Cow’s milk is a top food allergen and can provoke reactions ranging from digestive upset to severe allergic responses in sensitive individuals. Many people are also lactose intolerant, leading to gas, bloating, and diarrhea when consuming milk-containing products, and some may wish to limit saturated fat intake from full-fat dairy for cardiovascular health reasons.","category":"allergen (dairy)"}

soybean and wheat__food.analysis: {"name":"Soybean and wheat","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Soybean and wheat indicate the presence of both soy and wheat ingredients, which are common allergens. Wheat also contains gluten, which is problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.","details":"This labeling typically appears in allergen statements to highlight that the product contains or may contain soy and wheat components. Soy is a major allergen and can cause immune-mediated reactions in susceptible individuals, while wheat is also a top allergen and a primary dietary source of gluten. People with celiac disease, non-celiac gluten sensitivity, or wheat allergy must avoid wheat-containing products, and those with soy allergy must avoid soy; for others, these ingredients are generally safe in moderation.","category":"allergens (soy, wheat/gluten)"}

ingredients (label heading)__food.analysis: {"name":"Ingredients (label heading)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"The word “Ingredients” is a labeling heading and not an actual food ingredient. It is not consumed and has no nutritional or toxicological impact. It can be ignored when assessing the health and safety profile of the food product.","category":"not an ingredient"}
